question: After the config-reload title leak is fixed, should OpenClaw accept a bounded shared-SQLite `gateway_restart_audit` table that persists restart source, session fingerprint, and preflight metadata for gateway restart forensics?
rationale: This PR intentionally creates a new durable local audit surface for operational metadata, and automation cannot decide the acceptable long-term privacy and retention boundary for that data.

options.title: Repair then approve bounded gateway audit
options.body: Fix the remaining title leak, keep the 512-row local SQLite audit table, and require the redaction/retention tests to define the durable metadata contract.

options.title: Narrow the durable payload
options.body: Keep the table but remove or further coarsen preflight/session metadata so only reason/source/mode/timing fields persist.

options.title: Pause durable persistence
options.body: Decline the new table for now and keep restart attribution in non-durable logs or a narrower follow-up design.

recommendation.title: Repair then approve bounded gateway audit
recommendation.body: Fix the remaining title leak, keep the 512-row local SQLite audit table, and require the redaction/retention tests to define the durable metadata contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice is a product/security boundary over durable local metadata, and Peter Steinberger is a recurring restart/gateway refactor owner in the relevant history.
